meta.title: The private app for couples
meta.description: Nous Deux puts a couple's calendar, cycle, location and lists in one private space. Free, no ads, coming soon to the App Store and Google Play.

hero.line: An app for just the two of you. What you put in it stays between you.

agendas.heading: "What time are you home?"
agendas.body: Dinner at their parents' is in their calendar, the dentist is in yours, and in between there are a lot of texts to line things up.
agendas.body2: Nous Deux puts both lives on the same screen, and all it asks for is a six-character code.
agendas.caption: The shared calendar. Each event keeps the colour of whoever added it.
agendas.imageAlt: The Nous Deux shared calendar screen

merge.body: One of you generates a code, the other scans it. From then on, whatever one of you adds, the other sees.
merge.rightAlt: The calendar on your partner's phone
merge.mergedAlt: The same calendar, shared by two

share.heading: What you share
share.outro: No feed, no ads, no strangers.

items.name: Calendar
facts: Follows your phone's calendar and keeps it up to date.

items.name: Cycle
facts: A guide for each of you.

items.name: Location
facts: Live, when you turn it on.

items.name: Your days
facts: How many days you've been together.
A countdown to the next plan.

items.name: Little notes
facts: Thinking of you, good night, on my way.
Or your own words, sent with one tap.

items.name: Lists
facts: Ticked off on both phones, live.

trust.heading: Nobody else reads it.
points: There are no ads, and there never will be.
Your data isn't sold or used to target you.
Location has no history: only the latest one is kept.
If one of you leaves the couple, everything you shared is deleted.

items.question: Is it free?
items.answer: Yes, and there are no ads. If the app is useful to you, you can support the project with a coffee.

items.question: How do I invite my partner?
items.answer: In the app, generate a code and show it. Your partner scans it or types it, and you're linked straight away.

items.question: Who sees my data?
items.answer: Your partner, and nobody else in the app. It isn't sold or used for advertising. The privacy policy explains where it's hosted.

items.question: How do I delete my account?
items.answer: In the app: Settings › Account › Delete my account. Without access to the app, email the address on the Account deletion page, with the email address (Google or Apple) you sign in with.

items.question: When does the app come out?
items.answer: The beta is open on Android and iPhone: the "Join the beta" page explains how to install it. The App Store and Google Play launch will follow. The source code is already public on GitHub.

meta.title: Privacy policy
meta.description: What data Nous Deux collects and why, where it is stored (our own servers in Germany, in the EU), and how to use your rights.

editor.title: Publisher and contact
editor.body: Nous Deux is a free, ad-free app for couples: a shared calendar, period tracking, location sharing if you turn it on, lists and little notes. For any question about this policy or your data, contact us through the project repository:

dataCollected.title: Data we collect
dataCollected.intro: We only process the data the app needs to work and to share things with your partner.

items.label: Account and authentication
items.text: sign-in identifier (sign in with Google or with Apple) and the email address Google or Apple provides, if any. For the few accounts we create ourselves (app store review, testing): an email address and a password, stored only as a hash. If you sign in with Apple: a token from Apple, kept only to withdraw the app's access to your Apple ID when you delete your account.

items.label: Profile
items.text: display name, app language, profile picture (avatar), link to your partner when you form a couple.

items.label: Shared calendar
items.text: titles, descriptions, dates and times of the events you or your partner create, and the countdown option if you turn it on for an event. If you follow a calendar of your phone: the titles, dates and times of its events from last month to six months ahead, copied and kept up to date by your phone when you open the app, plus a random identifier of that phone and when it last synced. Nothing else from your calendar leaves your phone. Unfollowing a calendar removes its copies from last month on, and turning them all off removes every copy. Visible only within the couple.

items.label: Period tracking
items.text: if you choose to track your cycle: the start and end dates of your periods, how you feel each day if you note it (symptoms, mood, and states you write yourself, such as “Craving chocolate”) and your notes. This is health data. Your partner sees your dates and how you feel for as long as you share them: two switches in the Period tab, on by default, that you can turn off at any time. The states you write are stored and shared like the others: your partner only sees them if you share “How I feel each day”. The states you keep to find again from one day to the next stay on your phone; we only receive the ones you note for a day. Your notes are never shared: nobody but you can read them.

items.label: Location (optional)
items.text: if you enable location sharing, your real-time position (latitude, longitude) is used for display on the map. No location history is stored, and when you turn sharing off, your last position is erased.

items.label: Shared lists
items.text: list names, items, who added them and whether they are ticked. Visible only within the couple.

items.label: Little notes
items.text: the last little note each of you sent, so your partner can see it: its type and time, and its text if you wrote it yourself (40 characters at most). Each new note replaces the previous one: no history is kept. The notification for a note you wrote doesn't contain its text, so the text never goes through Google's or Apple's notification servers. The words you keep to send again later stay on your phone; we only receive the one you send.

items.label: Days together
items.text: the date your relationship started, which either of you can change.

items.label: Notifications
items.text: notification token (FCM) to send you the reminders you turn on (for example the reminder the evening before your partner's period), your partner's little notes, and word that their period started when they share their cycle.

items.label: Crash reports
items.text: when the app crashes or hits an unexpected error: what went wrong and where in the app's code, the app version, the phone's model and state (system version, memory, storage, battery, network), its language and time zone, and whether the app had just come back from the background. A report is built to say nothing about you: no account, name, phone number, email, IP address or location, and no screenshot. The app cleans its error texts of email addresses, phone numbers, identifiers and coordinates before sending them, and our server filters out IP addresses, email addresses and device identifiers again before storing anything.

items.label: Technical data
items.text: requested permissions (calendar, notifications, location, camera to scan your partner's QR code) and information needed for the app to work on your device.

purposes.title: Purposes of processing
purposes.body: The data is used to: provide and secure the service (sign-in, storage, sync); let you share within the couple (calendar, period tracking, lists, little notes, days-together counter, location if turned on); send the notifications you accepted; show the map (through OpenFreeMap) when location sharing is on; find and fix crashes and errors (crash reports).

legalBasis.title: Legal basis
legalBasis.body: Processing of data related to your account, your profile, the calendar, lists and little notes is necessary for the performance of the contract (use of the app). Cycle data is health data: we only process it with your explicit consent (Article 9(2)(a) GDPR), which you give by choosing to track your cycle in the app. We record when you gave it, and clear that record when you withdraw it. You can withdraw it at any time in Settings › Period: you stop tracking and can delete all your cycle data. Location sharing and push notifications are optional and also based on your consent; you can turn them off at any time in the app or device settings. Crash reports rely on our legitimate interest in keeping the app working (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR); they are limited to the technical details listed above, and you can object by contacting us.

hosting.title: Hosting and processors
hosting.intro: Data is hosted and processed by the following services, in line with their privacy policies and applicable rules (including GDPR where relevant):

items.label: Hetzner (Germany)
items.text: our own servers in Germany, running Supabase (open-source software): sign-in, database and profile photos, backed up every day over an encrypted connection to Hetzner storage in Finland. They also run GlitchTip (open-source software), which receives crash reports. This website is hosted there too, with no ads. It counts its visits with Umami, open-source software running on these servers: pages viewed, the site you came from, browser, system, device type, screen size, language, approximate country, region and city (worked out from your IP address, which isn't kept), with no cookies. The site's only cookie remembers your language. The data stays in the EU.

items.label: OpenFreeMap (Hyperknot Software, Hungary)
items.text: map tiles, from OpenStreetMap, shown when location sharing is on. To draw the map, your phone asks its servers for the areas on screen: no account, no cookies, and its logs don't keep your IP address, except error logs, deleted after 7 days. The service may go through the Cloudflare network.

items.label: Google and Apple
items.text: sign-in (Sign in with Google / Sign in with Apple); data processed by these services is governed by their own policies. During the iPhone beta, the app is distributed through TestFlight (Apple), which passes on crash reports and the feedback you choose to send.

retention.title: Retention
retention.body: Data is kept while your account is active. For location and little notes, only the latest value is kept, and your location is erased as soon as you stop sharing it. What you note while waiting for your partner (period dates, daily check-ins, events) is kept when you join their code: it moves into your couple, where your partner sees it under the same rules as the rest (your sharing switches for your cycle). If one of you leaves the couple, the couple's shared data (calendar, period dates and daily check-ins, location, lists, little notes and start date) is deleted for both of you; your cycle notes, which are yours alone, stay until you delete them. When you stop tracking your cycle, you can delete all your cycle data at once. When you delete your account (Settings › Account), your account, profile, photo and cycle notes are erased at once, and you leave the couple: its shared data is deleted for both of you. If you signed in with Apple, the app's access to your Apple ID is withdrawn at the same time. Wrong invite codes are recorded with your account to limit attempts to 5 every 10 minutes; they are deleted after that, at the latest with your account. Likewise, the time the app passed your Apple sign-in to the server is recorded to limit this to once a minute, then deleted the same way. Backups are kept for 14 days: once an account is deleted or one of you leaves the couple, the erased data also disappears from the backups within 14 days. Crash reports are deleted after 30 days and are not backed up.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.intro: Under the GDPR and applicable data protection law, you have the following rights:
rightsList: Right of access to your personal data
Right to rectification of inaccurate or incomplete data
Right to erasure (subject to legal obligations)
Right to object to certain processing
Right to withdraw your consent at any time, without affecting what was done before

meta.title: Account deletion
meta.description: How to delete your Nous Deux account and data, from the app or by email.

suppression.title: Account deletion
suppression.intro: You can delete your account yourself, from the app. It happens at once and can't be undone.
inAppSteps: On the Us tab, tap your initial or photo at the top right to open Settings.
Under Account, tap Delete my account.
Confirm. The app goes back to the sign-in screen.
suppression.deletedBody: Your account, profile, photo and cycle notes are erased at once. If you're in a couple, you leave it: your calendar, cycle, location, lists and little notes are deleted for both of you, and your partner keeps their account. Backups are kept for 14 days; after that, they no longer contain anything about you.
suppression.partialTitle: Deleting only some of your data
suppression.partialIntro: You can also erase some data from the app and keep your account:

partialItems.label: Your cycle
partialItems.text: in Settings › Period, turn off “I track my cycle in the app”, then choose Delete everything. Your period dates, daily check-ins and cycle notes are erased.

partialItems.label: One cycle
partialItems.text: on the Period tab, open Your cycles and long-press the one to delete.

partialItems.label: An event
partialItems.text: on the Calendar tab, long-press the event, then tap Delete. An event copied from a followed phone calendar is deleted on your phone, or removed by unfollowing that calendar.

partialItems.label: Lists
partialItems.text: swipe an item to the left to delete it, tap Clear all to remove ticked items, or delete the whole list from its options.

partialItems.label: Your location
partialItems.text: in Settings › Location, turn off “Share my location”. Your last position is erased.

partialItems.label: Everything you share
partialItems.text: in Settings › Couple, tap Leave couple. Your calendar, period dates and daily check-ins, location, lists, little notes and start date are deleted for both of you. Your cycle notes, which are yours alone, stay until you delete them.

suppression.partialNote: A deleted event or list item disappears for your partner too. Erased data leaves the backups within 14 days.
suppression.howToIntro: Write to the following address to ask for your account and personal data to be deleted:
suppression.phoneNote: In your message, include the email address (Google or Apple)
suppression.phoneNoteSuffix: you sign in with. That's how we find your account.

meta.title: Join the beta
meta.description: Try Nous Deux on Android or iPhone before it launches: Google Play for Android, TestFlight for iPhone.

beta.title: Join the beta
beta.intro: Nous Deux is being tested on Android and iPhone before its launch. It's free, with no ads, and your feedback shapes what comes next.

steps.text: Join the testers' group with the Google account on your phone.
Open the Google Play testing link with the same account and accept the invitation.
Install Nous Deux from Google Play and sign in with Google.
Your partner does the same with their own account. Then one of you generates a code and the other types it in, and you're paired.

beta.stayBody: Google only releases an app after a test of 14 days in a row with at least 12 testers. Keep Nous Deux installed and stay in the test for 14 days: that's what will let it open to everyone.
beta.languageBody: The app is in French and English only. If your phone isn't set to French, it shows in English.
beta.feedbackBody: A bug, an idea, a question? Write to us:
beta.dataBody: During the beta, the app works like the final version: your data is on our own servers in Germany and is never sold. You can delete your account from the app at any time. The testers' group runs on Google Groups: only its owner sees your address, and only to run the test. On iPhone, TestFlight is Apple's: it passes on crashes and the feedback you choose to send.
beta.leaveBody: On Android, open the Google Play testing link and choose "Leave the program"; you can also leave the testers' group. On iPhone, open Nous Deux in TestFlight and choose "Stop Testing".

iphoneSteps.text: Install TestFlight, Apple's app for testing apps, from the App Store.
On your iPhone, open the beta link and accept the invitation.
Install Nous Deux from TestFlight and sign in with Apple or Google.
Your partner does the same, on iPhone or Android. Then one of you generates a code and the other types it in, and you're paired.
